name: Ariadne Related Posts
author: Ucheagwu Onyike

sections.description:
Ariadne Related Posts surfaces genuinely related posts for any WordPress site, entirely on its own:

  • Shared tags — a capped, diminishing-returns tag-overlap score.
  • Shared categories — the same capped-overlap formula, independent of tags.
  • Title overlap — Jaccard similarity of stopword-stripped title tokens.
  • Local text matching — BM25 lexical scoring of each post’s body text, computed and cached on your own server.

Every signal’s weight is adjustable from the Settings screen. Nothing is scored live at page-render time — everything is precomputed on save and kept fresh by background jobs that continue processing on their own, without waiting on site traffic to trigger the next batch, so the plugin stays safe on sites with heavy traffic or full-page caching, and still finishes a large backfill promptly on a quiet site. Everything above runs 100% locally — no external service, no API key, no account, nothing to configure to get started.

Related posts display automatically, or place them yourself with a shortcode, a Gutenberg block, or a widget — your choice. A “Dashboard,” “Settings,” and “Post Status” admin screen (with an optional dark mode) show background-job progress and per-post status, and each post’s edit screen gets a meta box showing its current auto-computed related list, with scores, for transparency.

Pro & Pro+

Upgrading adds AI-powered semantic embeddings (Voyage AI), fused with the free local text signal via Reciprocal Rank Fusion for real body-text understanding beyond keyword overlap, plus WooCommerce/other post-type support, full Customizer style control, manual pin/exclude, Cornerstone Posts, a live-preview button that scores your unsaved draft before you publish, and more. Pro+ adds repeating boxes placed naturally inside the article body, settings export/import, and WP-CLI. See the in-plugin pricing page for the full breakdown.

External services

This plugin’s own scoring and matching (tags, categories, title overlap, local BM25 text matching) runs entirely locally — no data leaves your site for that. It uses the Freemius SDK for licensing, and two optional pieces load an external resource, under the conditions below:

Freemius (licensing) — this plugin uses the Freemius SDK to manage plugin updates and Pro/Pro+ license activation. It contacts the Freemius API (api.freemius.com) to check your license status and deliver updates; on activation, Freemius shows its own opt-in screen asking permission before any anonymous, non-personal diagnostic data (e.g. site URL, plugin/WordPress/PHP versions) is shared — this is optional and declining it does not affect the plugin’s functionality. See Freemius’s Privacy Policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/ and Terms of Service: https://freemius.com/terms/

Google Fonts (Pro/Pro+ only) — this plugin’s own Dashboard, Settings, and Post Status admin screens use a self-hosted typeface (DM Sans, bundled with the plugin) — nothing is requested from Google for those. Separately, if a Pro/Pro+ license is active and a site owner selects one of the curated Google Fonts for the related-posts card styling (Customizer), that one font family is requested from Google’s font CDN (fonts.googleapis.com) on your site’s frontend. No data beyond the standard browser request (e.g. IP address, user agent) is sent to Google. See Google’s Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy and Google Fonts’ own privacy FAQ: https://developers.google.com/fonts/faq/privacy

Voyage AI (Pro/Pro+ only) — if a Pro/Pro+ license is active and a site owner has entered their own Voyage AI API key, this plugin sends each post’s title and body text to the Voyage AI API (https://voyageai.com) once, when that post is saved and its content has changed, to compute a semantic-embedding vector used for the AI-matching signal. This is entirely opt-in (no key = no calls) and uses the site owner’s own account and key, not a shared or plugin-provided one. See Voyage AI’s Terms of Service: https://www.voyageai.com/tos and Privacy Policy: https://www.voyageai.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the ariadne-related-posts folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the “Plugins” screen in WordPress.
  3. Visit Settings → Ariadne Related Posts to adjust scoring weights, or just leave the defaults — it works immediately with zero configuration.
sections.faq:
Does this call any external service?

Not in the free version. Every signal (tags, categories, title overlap, and local BM25 text matching) is computed locally, with no external API calls, no account, and nothing to configure. Pro adds an optional AI-powered semantic-matching signal, which does call a third-party API (Voyage AI) using your own API key — entirely opt-in, and the plugin works fully without it.

Does this slow down my site?

No. Nothing is ever scored at page-render time. Every related-post list is precomputed in the background (in small, budgeted batches) and simply read from a cache when a page loads.

Can I control where the related-posts block appears?

Yes — auto-insert after your content, or place it yourself anywhere with the [ariadne_related] shortcode, the Gutenberg block, or a widget. (Pro adds choosing the exact paragraph it lands after, and Pro+ adds boxes placed naturally inside the article body.)

What happens to my settings if I downgrade from Pro/Pro+?

Nothing is lost. Anything that depends on a Pro/Pro+ feature (custom styling, pinned posts, etc.) simply stops being applied while locked — the underlying data stays saved, and everything picks back up automatically if you upgrade again.
sections.changelog:
1.9.56

  • Fixed: the two new “Related Posts” link-behavior options added in 1.9.55 (rel=”nofollow”, open in new tab) were placed inside the same Customizer section as the block’s Pro-only style controls, so — despite being intended as free, unconditional settings — they weren’t actually reachable without a Pro license. Moved to their own always-available “Related Posts: Link Behavior” section. Found via a real WordPress.org compliance pass against the downloaded free-build zip, not by re-reading the source.

1.9.55

  • Added: a public ariadne_related_post_ids filter — apply_filters( 'ariadne_related_post_ids', array $post_ids, int $post_id, int $count ) — lets a theme or another plugin see and adjust the final related-post list before it displays. Also adds a matching ariadne_get_related_post_ids( $post_id, $count = 0 ) function for reading that same (already-filtered) list directly.
  • Added: link attribute controls for the Related Posts block and the Inline Related Post feature (Customizer, free on every tier) — an option to add rel="nofollow" to related-post links, and an option to open them in a new tab. Opening in a new tab always adds rel="noopener" automatically alongside whatever nofollow is set to, regardless of tab setting.

1.9.54

  • Confirmed: fully compatible with WordPress 7.1.2 — verified admin pages, Customizer registration, the Related Posts block, REST routes, and a real post save/scoring pass all run clean with no errors, warnings, or deprecation notices.
  • Fixed: several CSS selectors (the Related Posts card image, and the Inline Related Post’s label and image) shared the exact same specificity as an ordinary theme rule — e.g. a theme’s own .prose img { height: auto } — so which one won a property like height: 100% came down to stylesheet load order rather than always favoring this plugin’s own styling. A theme rule loading after this plugin’s could silently win that tie, most visibly making the Related Posts card image fall back to its default square shape and spill down over the title below it. Every affected selector now includes its real, always-present wrapper element in the selector itself, so this plugin’s styling always outranks a same-shape theme rule regardless of load order.

1.9.53

  • Fixed: BM25 lexical scoring and the AI embeddings signal each pulled a candidate batch’s postmeta via update_meta_cache(), which caches every meta key WordPress finds for those posts — including the (often large) stored embedding vector, even for the BM25 pass that never reads it. Both now fetch only the specific meta key each signal actually needs, directly. On a real load test this cut scoring time for a 500-candidate pool from ~1.5s to under 250ms for BM25, and removed multi-second variance from the embeddings pass.
  • Fixed: publishing or updating a post could take multiple seconds longer than necessary, because the background-job “nudge” (a small internal request that keeps the sweep/backfill queue moving without waiting for site traffic) was sent synchronously in the middle of the save, and measured taking about a second per attempt in some environments — up to twice per save. It’s now deferred to run after the response has already been sent, and multiple nudges queued during one request are combined into one. A real bulk-import load test showed per-post save time drop by roughly 70% after this change.

1.9.52

  • Fixed: the Description, Pro & Pro+, External Services, and FAQ sections of this readme misattributed local BM25 text matching to Pro — it’s a free-tier signal and always ran locally regardless of license; only the AI (Voyage) embedding signal and its Reciprocal Rank Fusion with BM25 are actually Pro.

1.9.51

  • Fixed: a duplicate .arp-info-icon/.arp-info-tooltip CSS rule from the 1.9.49 System Health tooltips was overriding the original definition already used by the Settings page’s “Why is this locked?” tooltips — merged back into one shared, corrected rule (outline instead of filled, properly centered glyph) so both places benefit consistently.
  • Fixed: a two-word System Health row name (e.g. “New Matches”) could wrap to two lines at some content widths, which pushed the tooltip “i” icon down to sit between the lines instead of beside the first one. The icon now stays pinned to the first line regardless of wrapping.

1.9.50

  • Changed: “New Matches” row’s tooltip now says “…because a new post matched them” instead of “…because something new matched them.”

1.9.49

  • Added: “New Matches” row on the Dashboard’s System Health panel — reports when a newly-saved post discovers a match with an older post and queues that older post for a refresh, with a count and “how long ago.” Reuses the existing job-throughput log, no new background job.
  • Changed: “Related Post Lists” renamed to “List Freshness” — the old name read as “has related posts” when it actually means “is the computation current.”
  • Changed: every System Health row’s explanation moved from a description under the name to a hover/focus “i” tooltip — outline style, properly centered.
  • Removed: the “Background Processing” row — redundant with the page’s own “Background Jobs” section just below it, which already shows the same information per-job with real Last run/progress/manual-trigger detail instead of one aggregated Active/Idle state.

1.9.48

  • Added: “Edge-to-edge image” option for the Inline Related Post card (Customizer → Inline Related Post → Image) — the thumbnail bleeds to the card’s own left edge instead of sitting inset, matching the card’s corner radius. Mirrors the main block’s existing edge-to-edge feature (top-bleed for a vertical card), adapted for Inline’s horizontal row. Only offered for the Card/Boxed styles with a Square image shape.

1.9.47

  • Added: “Getting started checklist” toggle (Settings → General, free) — the only thing controlling whether the Dashboard’s onboarding checklist shows at all. On by default; stays visible whether or not the steps below it are finished, until a site owner turns it off.
  • Changed: dropped the checklist’s “Pick a layout” step — whether the Customizer’s layout setting differs from its default (‘row’) isn’t a reliable signal of intent, and read as a false “not done” on a Pro site that simply hadn’t changed it yet.

1.9.46

  • Added: a “Getting started” checklist on the Dashboard for first-time setup — reviewing the candidate pool, turning on auto-insert, setting the post count, and (Pro) picking a layout or adding a Voyage AI key. Every step reflects real settings state, not a separate dismissal flag, and the whole card disappears once the required steps are done.

1.9.45

  • Added: “Content priority” (Settings → General, free) — controls the priority of Related’s own the_content filter, for coexisting with another plugin that also inserts content into posts this way (e.g. an ad-insertion plugin). Distinct from “Custom ad-hook name,” which is for a theme’s own dedicated ad-placement hook outside the_content entirely.

1.9.44

  • Changed: “Posts to show” (how many related posts the block displays by default) is now a free setting on the Settings → General tab — previously only adjustable via the Customizer’s Pro-only Related Posts section, with no free-tier way to change the site-wide default (a post’s own per-post override was already free, just not the global default).

1.9.43

  • Added: a thin inline progress bar on each System Health row that represents a genuine percent-of-total metric (AI Summaries, Related Post Lists, AI Matching) — color always matches that row’s own status pill, never a separate palette.
  • Fixed: the Dashboard’s Refresh button had no dedicated styling and fell back to wp-admin’s default blue-accented button, clashing with the purple pill-shaped Dark mode toggle right next to it. Now styled as the same pill family.

1.9.42

  • Changed: Dashboard’s System Health/AI Usage row now gives the usage chart more visual weight relative to the health list, instead of an even split.
  • Added: a “Cornerstone Posts” report on the Dashboard — how many posts are currently pinned to always appear as related content sitewide, and a list of which ones, each linking to its edit screen.

1.9.41

  • Changed: every enqueued script/style handle (arp-admin, arp-style, arp-blocks, etc. — 11 handles, 19 registration/reference sites) was still the old short prefix; renamed to ariadne-* for the same WordPress.org naming-uniqueness reason as v1.9.38’s function/class/option rename. No visible change — same files, same behavior, just how they’re registered internally.

1.9.40

  • Fixed: the fix in 1.9.38 that stopped discarding a downgraded site’s saved style settings also accidentally removed the license check on the actual Google Fonts CDN request — a downgraded site now correctly keeps its stored font choice in its own card CSS without pinging Google’s servers for it, matching this readme’s own “Pro/Pro+ only” disclosure again.
  • Changed: two more admin page slugs (Settings, Post Status) were still the old arp--prefixed names; now consistent with the rest of the v1.9.38 rename.

1.9.39

  • Fixed: a stale shortcode example in this readme still showed the old [arp_related] name — now [ariadne_related], matching what’s actually registered.
  • Changed: the admin menu slug and Freemius menu config were the last two leftover arp--prefixed identifiers from the v1.9.38 rename; now ariadne-dashboard.

1.9.38

  • Fixed: a locked/downgraded site’s related-posts styling and Google Fonts selection were silently discarded and replaced with defaults at render time regardless of what was actually saved — settings are always honored now; only the Customizer controls to change them stay Pro-gated.
  • Fixed: this readme’s Voyage AI Terms/Privacy links (voyageai.com’s bare domain now redirect-loops; switched to www.voyageai.com).
  • Changed: internal function/class/option prefix renamed for WordPress.org’s naming-uniqueness guideline. Existing installs migrate settings, post data, and the internal cache automatically on upgrade — nothing user-facing changes.

1.9.34 – 1.9.37

  • Fixed: narrow-width panel spacing on Dashboard/Settings/Post Status; an int cast before a display value; a tier-check helper failing open for an undefined key; tightened settings-import file validation.
  • Added: this readme’s External Services section now discloses the Freemius SDK’s own license/update-check calls; bundled the DM Sans font’s OFL license text.
  • Changed: trimmed the header description; made a Preview panel help line tier-aware; internal build-hygiene follow-ups (no functional change).

1.9.33

  • Added: Post Status now has a combined “Status” column (Healthy / Needs update / Missing summary / Not using AI) and one-click filter shortcuts above the existing detailed filters.

1.9.31 – 1.9.32

  • Changed: the Dashboard’s Overview KPI row was folded into System Health (it repeated the same signals a second time); dark mode’s card borders are now a soft translucent highlight; several mobile-width layout gaps fixed.
  • Fixed: a “Quick Settings” card could link into a Customizer section unavailable on the current plan — a locked card now shows its required tier and links to upgrade instead.

1.9.29 – 1.9.30

  • Changed: Dashboard redesigned around what actually needs answering (health, attention, AI/API usage, background activity, configuration). Settings/Post Status also got a visual pass.

1.9.26 – 1.9.28

  • Changed: “Who can view reports” is now a free role-picker for every tier. Removed the Customizer’s Custom CSS field in favor of WordPress’s own Additional CSS. Admin UI refinement; addressed Plugin Check findings; fixed an incomplete uninstall cleanup.

1.9.18 – 1.9.25

  • Fixed: tag-matching scored zero for non-Post content types; a background job that could get stuck “Running…” with no manual restart.
  • Changed: several WordPress.org compliance fixes and admin UI polish (page width, status pills, dark-mode search, reduced-motion, keyboard accessibility).

1.9.0 – 1.9.17

  • Added: a chart hover tooltip, Voyage API call tracking, author exclusion, a per-signal score breakdown tooltip. Fixed the usage chart lagging a day behind. Rewrote the plugin description to lead with what Free actually does.

1.6.0 – 1.8.9

  • IMPORTANT: introduced the Free/Pro/Pro+ split — AI matching and inline related-post boxes became Pro/Pro+ only. Every Pro/Pro+ feature gained a license gate, then physical code-stripping from the Free build. The Ariadne brand mark, named position presets, a duplicate-insertion guard.

0.1.0 – 1.5.8

  • Early development history (multi-post-type support, Cornerstone Posts, the rename from “Echo Related Post” to “Ariadne Related Posts”, dark mode, and more) — full detail lives in this plugin’s version control.
